intro.text: Stagwell Inc. is the global challenger network transforming marketing through artificial intelligence (“AI”). Stagwell delivers scaled creative performance for the world’s most ambitious brands, connecting culture-moving creativity with leading-edge technology to harmonize the art and science of marketing. Led by entrepreneurs, our specialists in over 34 countries have a unified purpose: to drive effectiveness and improve business results for our more than 4,500 clients as of December 31, 2025. Since 2021, Stagwell’s standing in the industry has grown as customers have increasingly recognized our agencies’ outstanding work - leading to accelerating net new business trends - and as we have invested in augmenting our capabilities and geographical reach. Throughout our growth, we have maintained a collaborative spirit that is integral to the Stagwell DNA.

oi.heading: Operating Income
oi.text:
Operating Income for the year ended December 31, 2024, was $133.1 million, compared to $90.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2023, representing an increase of $42.5 million. The increase in Operating Income was primarily attributable to an increase in Revenue and a decrease in Impairment and other losses, partially offset by an increase in Cost of services, Office and general expenses, and Depreciation and amortization.

The increase in Cost of services was primarily attributable to higher billable costs and staff costs, commensurate with the increase in revenue as well as the inclusion of costs from acquired entities.

The increase in Office and general expenses was primarily attributable to an increase in staff costs, commensurate with the increase in revenue, the inclusion of costs from acquired entities and an increase in deferred acquisition consideration, partially offset by a decrease in stock-based compensation.

Stock-based compensation decreased $5.0 million, primarily due to a decrease in the fair value and number of awards, partially offset by an increase in the fair value of profits interest awards.

The Company expects to make estimated cash payments in the future to satisfy obligations under our Tax Receivables Agreement (“TRA”) , which remains in effect after the final exchange of Class C Common Stock (see Note 17 of the Notes included herein for additional details). The amount and timing of any payments under the TRA are contingent on the Company achieving certain tax savings, if any, that we actually realize, or in certain circumstances are deemed to realize. Based on the current outlook, the Company believes future cash flows from operations, together with the Company’s existing cash balance and availability of funds under the Credit Agreement, will be sufficient to meet the Company’s anticipated cash needs for the next twelve months and subsequent periods.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
